entries.title: Job 31:1
segments: Made a covenant with mine eyes; that they should look upon nothing that could excite impure desire.

entries.title: Job 31:2
segments:
What portion of God; what portion to one who transgresses his law. 
 
True religion leads those who have it to feel that the eye of God is upon them, and strive to regulate their appetites and passions, and all their thoughts and feelings, as well as their outward conduct, according to his will.

entries.title: Job 31:4
segments: He; God.

entries.title: Job 31:5
segments:
Hasted to deceit; to execute a deceitful or fraudulent purpose. 
 
Piety towards God will lead to justice, impartiality, and kindness towards men; to honesty, chastity, diligence, sobriety, and all those virtues which promote the welfare of individuals and of the community.

entries.title: Job 31:6
segments: Let me be weighed in an even balance; be righteously judged.

entries.title: Job 31:7
segments: If any blot hath cleaved to my hands; if he had committed any crime.

entries.title: Job 31:9
segments: Laid wait; to commit adultery with his neighbor's wife.

entries.title: Job 31:11
segments:
Punished by the judges; it is an offence not only against individuals but against society, and as such to be punished by the magistrates. 
 
Infidelity to the marriage covenant is a great crime, and those who are guilty of it are among the basest and most mischievous of men.

entries.title: Job 31:13
segments:
If I did despise the cause of my man-servant or--maid-servant; if he had not been strictly impartial and just towards them, as well as towards his equals. 
 
Servants and masters have the same heavenly Parent, and are brethren; and they are bound to treat each other as such, doing, each to the other, as they ought to wish that the other should do to them.

entries.title: Job 31:14
segments: Riseth up; to judgment.

entries.title: Job 31:15
segments: Make him; we had one common Creator, have one common nature, and are brethren.

entries.title: Job 31:16
segments:
Their desire; what they ought to desire and might reasonably expect. 
 
True religion is compassionate, and leads those who have it to assist the widow and the fatherless, the poor, the sick, and the destitute, and in various ways, as they have opportunity and ability, to help the needy.

entries.title: Job 31:18
segments:
Her; the widow. 
 
  From my mother's womb; from his earliest years.

entries.title: Job 31:21
segments:
Saw my help in the gate; saw those ready to aid and abet me before the magistrate in any course I might take.  The gate is mentioned as the place where courts were held. 
 
Piety in magistrates will lead to fidelity in the discharge of official duties; will secure the weak and helpless against the encroachments of the strong and overbearing; and will afford protection to the just rights of all.

entries.title: Job 31:23
segments: Could not endure; to oppress the fatherless; he was kept from it by the fear of God.

entries.title: Job 31:24
segments: The increase of riches increases the danger of setting the heart on them; and men are often secretly idolaters, without publicly bowing down to idols.  They deny to God the homage of their hearts, and live without loving or obeying him.

entries.title: Job 31:27
segments:
Secretly enticed; to worship any of the heavenly bodies. 
 
  Kissed my hand; a form of idolatrous worship.

entries.title: Job 31:29
segments: Lifted up myself; been elated, and rejoiced when evil came upon his enemy.

entries.title: Job 31:31
segments: Oh that we had of his flesh!--cannot be satisfied; or, as some render, "Where is one who was not satisfied from his flesh?"

entries.title: Job 31:32
segments: It is exceedingly difficult for a man to recount his virtues and not be elated, and it is ordinarily not best to attempt it; yet sometimes it is proper, and if done with a right spirit, may be useful; but much grace is needful to prevent being so lifted up with pride as to fall into the condemnation of the devil.

entries.title: Job 31:33
segments: Hiding mine iniquity; from men, and trying to hide it from God.

entries.title: Job 31:34
segments:
That I kept silence; when he should have spoken. 
 
  Went not out; from fear of the contempt of his neighbors.  Some have supposed the meaning of this verse to be, Let me be confounded before the multitude, let the contempt of families follow me, let me be silent and not go abroad, if I have covered my transgressions, or committed any of the crimes above-mentioned.

entries.title: Job 31:35
segments: Written a book; written out the charges against him, that he might understand and answer them; have a fair trial, and be acquitted.

entries.title: Job 31:36
segments: Take it upon my shoulder; sustain his innocence, and in such a manner that all might see it.  He would even wear the disproved accusation as an ornament.

entries.title: Job 31:37
segments: As a prince would I go; with confidence to be acquitted and approved; not as a criminal to be condemned.

entries.title: Job 31:38
segments: If my land cry against me; for having wrongfully obtained it, or not justly rewarding those who have cultivated it.

entries.title: Job 31:39
segments:
Without money; without fully paying for it, or for the labor bestowed upon it. 
 
  Caused--to lose their life; by taking away their means of support. 
 
To withhold a just reward from the laborer, or eat the fruit of his toil without compensation, is a heinous sin; and though it may be hidden from men, it will be brought to light by God, and be visited with his sore displeasure.

entries.title: Job 31:40
segments:
Thistles--and cockle; noisome weeds. 
 
  The words of Job are ended; his discussion with his friends.  He speaks afterwards only in two short prayers and confessions to God.
